requirements.description: Trace cli.ts, AskCommand.ts, RunCommand.ts, CodaliRuntime, CodaliJobRuntime, SmartPipeline and CodaliGateway to all provider/tool calls, including summarization, repair, Docdex delegation and media. Produce a current call map, enumerate every model-binding source and choose the outer lifecycle owner for terminal sessions. Preserve embedded-host behavior.
Reindex affected source and repair/verify Docdex graph coverage. Record current tests, package exports, Node support, config precedence and public API consumers.

With a dedicated test account/workspace, probe mSwarm discovery, quotas, streaming, cancellation, idempotency and job-status behavior on both Raijin and Suku. Inventory Strata-served text models plus smaller, embedding, audio, image and video models; verify placement, entitlement, revisions, supported operations/formats/limits, native reasoning, embedding compatibility and synchronous/asynchronous behavior. Verify each actual transport/adapter rather than assume installation means Codali integration.

Run a small baseline corpus through current Codali. Capture success, tool validity, queue time, latency, tokens and failure modes. Record production traffic baselines for TNL/BDYA/Logmira before adding CLI load.

Write decisions for execution location, one orchestration owner, terminal renderer, session storage migration, config/key precedence, permission enforcement and platform isolation. Freeze initial event/API fixtures and a capability matrix.

Define the shared orchestration-config schema and migration from existing agent/provider settings. Produce a Raijin/Suku profile and alternate-deployment fixture; specify all internal model bindings, fallback rules, optional disabled capabilities and turn-boundary upgrades.

Refresh the read-only hardware/residency audit in Section 4.4 and extend it with controlled peak-memory measurements under text, retrieval, vision and media workloads. The selected qualification profiles are SERA-14B Q4_K_M on Suku GPU1 and Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 Q4_K_M on Raijin GPU1, with SERA-8B as a Suku alternative. Preserve the measured reservations/guards and validate production coexistence; the passive baseline alone does not qualify an installation.

Map SessionStore, CodaliGatewayStore, CodaliJobRuntime and mcoda TaskOrderingService/TaskStateService. Choose the authoritative owner and adapters for standalone versus project-attached work. Freeze GoalContract, PlanRevision, TaskContract, DecisionRecord, EvidenceReceipt and Checkpoint examples; document status mapping, versioning and durability. No second mutable backlog or outer agent loop.

Turn this accepted build plan into requirement-to-task-to-evidence fixtures and choose the tracked documentation destination. Establish the long-task baseline from Section 11: goal retention, missed requirements, scope drift, architecture violations, failed handoffs, duplicate work and false completion. Include bounded planning-only evaluations before qualifying smaller planners.

Add mSwarm login/logout/status using the existing credential resolver, masked interactive entry, stdin for automation and environment-based injection. Implement rotation and removal without logging keys.

Normalize mSwarm catalog entries for both hosts, distinguishing text, embedding, image, audio and video operations, revisions, backend identity and resource pools. Intersect discovery with configured approved models and account entitlements; cache with expiry per endpoint/account. Never silently add an unconfigured model or reuse another account's catalog after changing keys.
Integrate the existing runtime usage-limits endpoint. Distinguish authentication failure, missing model entitlement, quota exhaustion, account service outage and model unavailability.

Expand doctor to check package version, supported runtime, credential presence/validity, endpoint trust, catalog, required routes, Docdex and platform executor capabilities. Keep useful local diagnostics available offline.
Specify setup's package/install behavior and backward-compatible configuration migration. Fix dev version output and stale help/README claims.

Implement the shared orchestration-config schema/loader/validator and effective-config inspection. Route CLI, embedded-host and background-job resolution through it; migrate existing settings with explicit diagnostics rather than preserve hidden defaults. Validate capability bindings and fallback chains, keep secrets indirect, and stamp resolved versions/hashes on requests.

Validate task-control policies with the same loader: bounded planning/review depth, concurrency, retries, checkpoints and escalation. Policies may narrow hard safety invariants; they cannot enable additional workspace writers, disable required completion evidence or expand account permissions. Expose resolved values without a model call.

Introduce the session controller around the chosen existing orchestration path. Define start turn, steer, queue input, cancel, inspect and checkpoint operations. Maintain compatibility adapters for legacy CLI and embedded runtime calls.
Extend typed runtime/provider events with stable identity, ordering, final-state rules, bounded buffers and backpressure. Persist important events through SessionStore.
Thread cancellation/deadlines through providers, remote invocation control, subagent scheduling and pending tool work. Distinguish cancel-requested from confirmed cancelled.
Add a shared budget object and usage accumulator at the controller boundary. Every nested model/tool call reserves from it before starting.
Add basic crash-safe checkpoints and event replay using fake providers and a plain text/JSONL harness. Keep writing tools disabled until Phase 3's gate passes.

Extend the common tool/job envelope for media submission, durable remote IDs, progress, artifact references and cancellation reconciliation. Keep model bindings/configuration pinned for in-flight jobs; binary payloads do not enter text event logs.

Implement durable goal/requirement/decision/plan/task records and atomic revision checks, reusing P0.8's chosen storage boundaries. Include standalone sessions and project task adapters, idempotent projections and crash recovery. Distinguish invocation success from verified task/goal completion.

Add deterministic dependency validation/readiness and guarded task transitions. Validate coverage, missing/cyclic prerequisites, ownership and goal/plan versions. Apply steering atomically; invalidate incompatible queued tasks and reject stale results. Reserve budget for required validation.

Add headless inspect/amend/checkpoint commands and the evidence completion gate using fake providers. Prove a falsely confident model cannot complete an unmet criterion. Small tasks use the same records with minimal planning ceremony.

Implement the central allow/deny/ask gate and approval response contract, including persisted scoped grants and current-policy rechecks immediately before side effects. Integrate existing GatewayPolicyCompiler/ToolRegistry controls rather than bypassing them.

Replace the blocking shell path with an asynchronous process runner. Stream bounded stdout/stderr, record exit/signal state, support cancellation and process-group cleanup, enforce time/output limits, and define owned background process behavior. Preserve the existing tool contract where possible.

Implement and test Linux/macOS isolation adapters. Validate filesystem and network boundaries against interpreter execution, shell scripts, hooks, package managers and child processes. Do not rely on destructive-command pattern matching.

Apply the gate to file writes, patches, MCP/HTTP tools, Docdex mutations, media generation/artifact handling and subagents. Unknown external tools require explicit permission until classified. Network-read permission is separate from upload, metered generation and an external write action; existing image readOnly metadata cannot bypass policy.
Add workspace locks, file preconditions and tool intent/receipt records. Tests cover symlinks, path traversal, changed file contents, overlapping edits and partial failures.

Add the repository baseline/diff ownership ledger, task path/goal-version preconditions and scoped scratch cleanup. Wire required architecture/public-contract checks and trusted verification receipts into result acceptance. A helper, shell command or generated document cannot mutate authoritative work state outside its validated API.
Implement setup/doctor integration for local Docdex health, version, repository binding, initial index and incremental refresh. Use the existing client and registration flows.
Wire the standard coding workflow to search, symbols/AST, precise reads and impact analysis, with output/context budgets. Treat index health as part of the tool result.
Expose configured web research, source attribution and timeouts. Preserve operation allowlists and the difference between local and managed encrypted repositories.
Integrate agent profile and repository memory with separate read/write permissions and retention. Include provenance in context and prevent tool text from rewriting policy.
Expose trusted MCP/HTTP connectors and per-tool health. Failure of one optional connector must not disable unrelated local tools.

Integrate discovered embedding services through the supported Docdex/provider contract. Pin embedding-space identity per index, batch incrementally with cancellation, implement compatible-replica failover and rebuild/switch behavior for incompatible changes, and account for query versus background indexing usage.

Reuse ImageGenerationTool and GenerativeOperation contracts to expose configured image/audio/video creation tools. Add missing adapters and capability-specific validation, with supported conditioning/reference inputs and operation limits drawn from configuration plus inventory.

Implement durable media jobs and artifact storage/download/receipt handling, with bounded payloads, tenant isolation, safe paths, checksums, expiry/retention and explicit preview/export. Exercise mixed workflows that create and integrate code plus media without a separate planner.

Build bounded active-task context from canonical goal/plan records plus Docdex facts, profile, diary/wakeup and decision references. Implement freshness/contradiction handling, critical-context reservation and source-linked checkpoint summaries. Keep task state and authorization outside probabilistic memory retrieval.

Bind text roles, retrieval and media tools through the shared orchestration configuration and existing agent resolution. Enforce this deployment's Strata-backed large-Qwen rules during dispatch/pool expansion/fallback; prove another deployment profile can choose other supported models without engine changes.

Add bounded helper capsules, output schemas, source references and validation/escalation rules. Start with extraction/classification before enabling patch drafting. Never let a helper approve a privileged action.
Implement the four effort profiles with shared counters, account caps and requested/effective reporting. Add native reasoning mapping only for empirically supported adapters.

Integrate queue/admission/cancel status, cross-host routing and physical-pool concurrency, including large/small/embedding/media contention and loading peaks. Preserve interactive capacity while scheduling heavy video jobs. Fail over only after reconciling whether an invocation was already admitted; avoid duplicate renders and retry amplification.

Evaluate eligible large-model-only baselines versus offloaded runs on the same held-out tasks, recording model/host placement so routing changes do not confound the comparison. Tune helper eligibility, thresholds, context packing and review depth. Preserve source facts when small-model summaries are wrong or incomplete.

Qualify the two primary profiles from Section 4.4 first: SERA-14B Q4_K_M on Suku GPU1 within a 12-GiB process reservation plus 4-GiB guard, and Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 Q4_K_M on Raijin GPU1 within 4 GiB plus a 2-GiB guard. Start at 8K context/one slot/Q8 KV. Compare the 4B candidate against resident 4B Instruct and SERA against the configured lead/worker baseline; record TypeScript task quality, full-task latency and actual loading/prefill/generation peaks. SERA-8B on Suku is a replacement alternative, not another concurrent resident.

Implement shared GPU1 admission and media drain/unload/reload before enabling Suku's specialist. During rollout, install one candidate at a time using pinned verified artifacts, stable GPU UUIDs and disabled-until-qualified configuration entries; canary before promotion. Re-run compatibility, production/vision/media coexistence and configuration-only rollback tests. Reject or resize profiles whose measured peaks breach reservations; retain existing models if the new candidates do not improve the workload.

Implement scoped worker capsules/results, controller-issued attempt leases/fencing, deduplication, side-effect reconciliation on expiry and bounded progress detection. Preserve one writing task per worktree; use parallel helpers only where independent work and resource limits allow.

Evaluate planning/architecture/goal retention separately from coding. Compare lead-only execution, qualified helper decomposition and separate review on the same corpus/budgets. Measure constraint loss, invented tasks/APIs, ordering errors, rework and completion quality; remove optional stages that add cost without benefit. Use configured role bindings for all calls.

Implement the required default TUI: structured scrollable transcript, persistent multiline prompt editor, workspace/session/status area, searchable commands, history search and @file completion; preserve plain/JSONL modes, resize and terminal restoration.
Implement the alpha command set from Section 6 against controller state. Status and permission inspection must not trigger an inference call.
Build approval cards with concrete operation, paths/command, reason and grant scope. Build actual-diff and tool-output views with truncation/expansion controls.
Make steering, queued messages, cancellation and busy-state slash commands explicit. Display phase, actual model/node route, effort, context and queue state without flooding the screen.
Stabilize scripted mode: JSONL event output, final result format, stderr diagnostics and documented exit codes. Retain old command behavior and add migration notes.

Add /artifacts and media-job detail to /tasks, with artifact paths/provenance, separate render usage and explicit download/open actions. Surface effective model bindings/configuration version, pending configuration updates and modality-specific unsupported-operation errors.

Add /goal, /decisions and the expanded /plan and /tasks commands. Show current requirements, scope history, phase/task dependencies, blockers, ownership and evidence counts through deterministic reads. Make user steering reviewable with a plan diff; preserve authorization for routine work and make planning/execution mode changes explicit.

Qualify the required TUI with deterministic visual/input tests and real Linux/macOS PTY flows covering stream/redraw, Unicode, narrow resize, paste, completion, approval, busy steering/queueing, signals and resume; inspect exact-version visual fixtures.
Complete resume/fork/compaction and storage migration. Reconcile uncertain tool outcomes before continuing. Test stale repository state and multiple clients opening the same session.
Reconcile local usage with server invocation/account records, including retries, cancelled requests, delayed usage and reconnects. Show unknown/estimated values honestly.
Complete /context, /review and redacted export; expand /tasks recovery/evidence views and configuration provenance. Make active/background work ownership visible on exit/resume.
Add local retention/delete controls, diagnostic redaction, crash reporting that is opt-in and test-only telemetry fixtures. Do not silently enable existing dataset collection.

Run longer coding sessions against each selected model's actual context limit, including cross-host failover to a smaller compatible context window. Verify compaction preserves task constraints, pending work and validation evidence, and resume retains the pinned embedding-space identity.

Recover a render completed while the CLI was disconnected, refresh an expired artifact reference and migrate/roll back a model configuration without resubmitting active jobs. Preserve media provenance, accounting and artifact integrity across resume/export.

Run the long-task/fault corpus from Section 11 with repeated compaction, fresh contexts, restarts, steering, failed dependencies and user edits. Verify requirement/decision continuity, evidence invalidation, no duplicate side effects, useful next-task selection and honest blocked/partial outcomes. Run selected multi-hour live journeys on both hosts.

Run the release matrix across text, smaller, embedding, image, audio and video services on both hosts, including newly qualified specialists, background indexing and peak render allocations. Measure existing tenants under mixed CLI traffic, cold model loads and either-host failure; prove no OOM-driven eviction or starvation.
Fix admission, starvation, cancellation, stale leases and retry behavior demonstrated by those tests. Drain remote jobs before node upgrades and reconcile in-flight records afterward.
Build reproducible package artifacts and install-test the tarballs on clean supported systems. Verify package files, executable permissions, version/help output, migration and uninstall behavior.

Deploy additive backend changes before clients that need them. Gate incompatible capabilities explicitly. Publish a prerelease package, then promote the tested artifact after the canary gates pass. Do not select a future version number until release time.

Roll out to internal keys, a small opted-in cohort, then general availability. Keep switches for interactive mode, helper offloading and new routing behavior independently reversible. Pin the known-good previous client/backend versions and test downgrade readers before enabling a new session schema.

Publish the requirement-to-evidence report and failure taxonomy for the tested release. Exercise diagnosis from one user-visible stalled task to goal/plan versions, decisions, model/tool receipts and actionable recovery. Track architecture drift, scope changes, user corrections and false-completion incidents alongside latency/cost; gate optional stages/models on measured value.
